criteria.criterion: A test builds the text from each steward-channel writer (structural pass, design review, introspection follow-up, and any other writer found building a steward request) and runs it through the same acceptance and files parse that `athena plan` uses. None is refused for missing acceptance and each yields a non-empty file list. Run `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: steward_requests_from_every_writer_pass_the_plan_parse passed. It covers structural_text, design_review_text, RequestQueue::apply with a bare model request and a full one (introspection follow-ups reach the queue through the steward's ProposedChange.request), and blind_spot_change for every source. Each text goes through reading::request_text_acceptance and request_text_touches, which plan_entry now calls, and PlanEntry::missing() does not report acceptance. I grepped for writers: the only other request writers are Athena::queue/ask, which are CLI paths, and RequestQueue::apply, which is the only place a request is built on the REQUEST_CHANNEL ('steward').

criteria.criterion: A test builds a structural-pass request for a fixture file over each limit. The text has an `Acceptance:` section whose `- ` bullets name the breached limits as measured (lines, function length, weekly landings). The bullets also say no behavior change with existing tests passing, and that fmt, clippy and test pass. The text has a `Files:` line naming the file. Run `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: structural_text_lists_acceptance_naming_the_breached_limits passed. Its fixture breaches file length, function length and the busy-file limit. It asserts bullets with '2500 production lines, over the limit of 2000', 'function sprawl is 230 lines...', '6 landings in the last 7 days', 'No behavior change; the existing tests pass' and 'fmt, clippy and test pass'. It also asserts '\nFiles: crates/x/src/huge.rs\n'.

criteria.criterion: A test queues a structural pass for a file over its limits and closes that job. The next hook run (`code_health_after_landing`) queues a new structural pass for the same file. Run `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: structural_pass_is_queued_again_after_the_old_one_is_closed passed. It runs code_health_check, sees a second run queue nothing, closes the job as Rejected, then sees the next run queue a new job for the same path, with only the new one open. The test calls code_health_check, the body of the hook. The separate test note_finished_checks_code_health_after_a_landing_and_only_then covers the hook wiring, and it passed.

criteria.criterion: A single shared builder for steward requests exists, and every steward-channel writer constructs its text through it. A writer cannot omit `Acceptance:` bullets or `Files:`. The code or tests make this enforced rather than relying on convention.
criteria.evidence: StewardRequest in steward.rs has a private field. new() rejects empty or blank acceptance, an empty or non-path file list, a multi-line title, and body lines the plan parse would read as bullets. It then re-checks the rendered text with the plan parse. structural_text, design_review_text and blind_spot_request call new(). RequestQueue::apply, the single steward-channel record writer, calls from_change, so model-written introspection follow-ups cannot skip the builder. The builder tests and the all-writers test passed.

criteria.criterion: Closed, including refused, earlier structural passes count as not open in the dedupe. A still-open pass for the same file still suppresses a duplicate, and the existing test for that keeps passing.
criteria.evidence: structural_pass_open already treated any JobState::Closed as not open, and the logic is unchanged. Only the doc comment changed, and the new test pins the behaviour. A refused pass is not open once a person closes it, which matches the request ('closing the old refused passes lets the hook queue them again'). structural_pass_queues_nothing_for_a_file_with_an_open_request still passes.

criteria.criterion: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` all pass.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks on this tree: fmt passed, clippy with -D warnings passed, and cargo test --locked passed with 1327 tests.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the steward request format fix and the dedupe change.
criteria.evidence: The diff adds two entries under Fixed. One covers the StewardRequest builder, the Acceptance and Files format, the structural-pass bullets, the design-review body change and the all-writers test. The other covers reopening after close in the dedupe. It says honestly that the dedupe behaviour 'is tested'.

findings.summary: The code-health hook still writes through the general Athena::queue(&str), so a future code-health writer could pass raw text and skip StewardRequest.
findings.evidence: code_health_check calls self.queue(&structural_text(file)) and self.queue(&design_review_text(...)). Athena::queue takes any string, and the all-writers test only catches writers it lists. RequestQueue::apply, the steward-channel path, is fully enforced.

findings.summary: The reopen-after-close test documents behaviour that was already there and would also pass on the base tree.
findings.evidence: structural_pass_open's logic (!matches!(job.state(), JobState::Closed(_))) is unchanged in the diff, and the CHANGELOG states this accurately ('is tested to treat').

findings.summary: Code-health requests are queued on the 'cli' channel, not 'steward', so the request's description of them as steward-channel is not literally accurate. They are fixed anyway.

summary: The change fixes the problem where the writers create the requests. One shared builder, StewardRequest in steward.rs, renders an Acceptance: section of '- ' bullets and a Files: line, then re-checks the text with the parse athena plan uses. That parse is now extracted from plan_entry into reading.rs with no change in behaviour. The structural pass, design review, blind spot, and every steward-queued model request (including introspection follow-ups, through RequestQueue::apply) are built with it. Structural-pass bullets name each breached limit with its measured numbers, plus no behaviour change and fmt/clippy/test passing. The dedupe already counted closed passes as not open, and a new test now pins that it queues again after a pass is closed. I ran the targeted tests (steward_request: 3 passed; code_health: 17 passed). Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test runs pass. Every changed file is within the expected deliverables. One minor point: the code-health hook still queues through the general string-taking Athena::queue, so a future code-health writer could skip the builder unless the all-writers test is extended. Verdict: pass.
